reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes passive income through Uniswap and instructs viewers to deploy a bot and transfer at least 0.2 ETH to its contract address. It ties the requested funding to claims that the bot can front-run another transaction's slippage and profit, with larger contributions enabling larger transactions. Although the speaker acknowledges that profits fluctuate, the available video evidence describes a direct solicitation based on those profit claims.

citations.quote: I'll be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap.
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
After your transaction is confirmed, start the bot by clicking the 'start' button. Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal'
the more you put in, the larger the transaction you will be able to front run. And the more profit you will be able to accumulate over time.
This will allow our transaction to be processed first and then we'll also send a sell order within the same block.

opening.argument: The presentation does not offer a fixed or guaranteed return. It expressly warns that profitability varies from week to week, and it explains that token burn fees and insufficient funding can waste gas rather than generate profit. Those qualifications are material risk disclosures, not the language of a risk-free promise. The operational recommendation to fund the contract is framed around covering possible execution costs and slippage, while the viewer is told that results depend on the transactions and tokens encountered. A careful reading therefore supports a conditional, speculative trading demonstration with explicit downside warnings, rather than deceptive certification that every participant will profit.

citations.quote: Sometimes it's not always profitable and profits fluctuate week to week.
If you fund the contract with 0.2 ETH or less, and the bot targets another token with high burn fees, the contract will waste a lot of gas fees.
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes funding and profit language but omits the express qualification that results are not constant. “Passive income” describes the intended convenience of automation, not a guarantee, while the funding instruction is tied to slippage and transaction costs. The account of profits is presented alongside an admission that profitability fluctuates, so it cannot fairly be treated as an unconditional promise.

citations.quote: Sometimes it's not always profitable and profits fluctuate week to week.
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
I'll be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer about fluctuating results does not neutralize the central solicitation. The audience is still told to deposit ETH into a contract, start it, and expect profits, including claims of substantial gains. The fee warning explains why more funding may be needed; it does not establish that the contract is safe or that the claimed returns are independently verified.

citations.quote: Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
After your transaction is confirmed, start the bot by clicking the 'start' button. Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal'
But usually I make 2 plus Ethereum a week.

opening.argument: The primary format is a technical tutorial about deploying and operating a Solidity smart contract. The speaker explains MetaMask, Remix, compiler version selection, deployment, gas confirmation, contract controls, and checking the resulting address. That is concrete instruction about blockchain tooling and transaction workflow, not merely a request for money. The front-running concept is also explained as a mechanism involving pending transactions, gas priority, and same-block execution. The video can therefore be understood as an operational demonstration of MEV technology, with personal results included as an example rather than the sole subject. Its central viewer task is learning how the tool is built and used.

citations.quote: In this YouTube video tutorial, I'll be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap.
Under Compiler, select the version 0.6.6 so it will match our contract.
remix. Which is a web application that allows us to develop, deploy, compile, and launch smart contracts
The last step is to click start.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not make the content a solicitation. The actual sequence is technical: create a Solidity file, compile it to a specified version, deploy through Remix, and interact with contract controls. The explanation of front-running supplies the subject matter being demonstrated. Profit examples are contextual evidence of the demonstrated tool, while the format remains instructional and operational.

citations.quote: remix. Which is a web application that allows us to develop, deploy, compile, and launch smart contracts
Under Compiler, select the version 0.6.6 so it will match our contract.
This will allow our transaction to be processed first and then we'll also send a sell order within the same block.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical steps are the delivery mechanism for the financial pitch, not a separate neutral lesson. The tutorial tells viewers to deploy the contract, fund it, start it, and withdraw claimed profits. Its explanation specifically describes profiting from another transaction’s slippage, so the instructional framing cannot erase the direct financial inducement.

citations.quote: After your transaction is confirmed, start the bot by clicking the 'start' button. Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal
the victims transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we make a profit from the slippage difference in the transaction.
And the more profit you will be able to accumulate over time.

opening.argument: The evidence does not show a request for passwords, seed phrases, account credentials, recruitment, a membership fee, or a guaranteed payout. Instead, it describes a user-controlled contract workflow: deploy code, confirm blockchain transactions, activate the bot, and use a withdrawal control. The amount is not presented as a mandatory purchase price or subscription; the speaker says viewers can fund the contract with whatever amount they want. The material also identifies ordinary execution risks, including gas fees and token burn fees. On this record, the conduct is more consistent with promoting a software-based trading service or workflow whose performance depends on market conditions than with proving a conventional scam mechanism.

citations.quote: You can fund the contract with whatever amount you want,
The bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and anything lower.
Sometimes it's not always profitable and profits fluctuate week to week.
Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a password request or recruitment scheme is not decisive. This model's alleged risk is the transfer of ETH to a contract, and the prosecution identifies that funding instruction directly. A voluntary amount can still be a solicitation, and the described withdrawal control does not independently establish that funds will be returned. The operational terminology should not substitute for evidence of actual performance.

citations.quote: Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
You can fund the contract with whatever amount you want,
Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam need not request credentials or recruit a downline. Here, the requested asset is ETH itself, transferred to a contract, and the funding is linked to claims that larger deposits enable larger front-runs and more profit. Describing a withdrawal button and variable results does not show that users can actually recover their funds or that the bot performs as claimed.
